The rows a month's report speaks about, with their creator and their date

report_rows.Rd

A row counts while it is an access: request_status is active and outcome is applied. The filter is on the request and not on the outcome alone, because a revocation the round carried out closes with applied too; and any other outcome is not an access, and has had its own mail already.

Usage

report_rows(register, creators, executions, period, since = NULL, born = NULL)

Arguments

register

The register as read.

creators

Who created each row, as log_creators() answers, in the register's order.

executions

One element per row, in the register's order: what report_executions() answered, or NULL where the log was not read.

period

What report_month() answered.

since

One element per row, what report_person_since() answered, or NULL to date the person by the row's first execution.

born

When each row was made, as report_born() answers, in the register's order; NULL when unknown.

Value

The kept rows of register, with creator, attivata_il, nel_mese, senza_data, data_motivo, persona_dal and creata_il added.

Details

Of those, a row activated after the month covered waits for the next report, and every other one is kept. nel_mese says what the month did to it: attivata when its first execution falls in the month, modificata when it was executed again in the month after a change, "" otherwise.

A row whose log was read and does not date it is kept with senza_data: it is applied and the log does not say since when, which is a question for IT. data_motivo says which of the two ways: senza_sigillo, no seal written by the channel; log_ambiguo, the channel's fields written by more than one account, so that which one executed the row is unknown. The two send IT to look for different things. A row whose log could not be read is left out, since it cannot be judged on a reading that did not happen; the caller sends nothing on such a day.
